quotes.text: We have to win this arms race. [...] We can't allow AI to just go insane. Congress has to have some type of overarching regulatory environment to try to keep humans in charge of what goes on with AI. [...] I think the important thing is to make sure that humans are always in the loop, always in charge of this.

We're in a battle with artificial intelligence. Fortunately, we're ahead right now. But if they ever get ahead, our world changes completely. And data centers are the boogeyman. But if we don't have some way of computing all that artificial intelligence, we can't compete with them.

The integration of AI into medicine will revolutionize health care as we know it.

Thank you to the Connected Health Initiative and Duke AI Health for hosting me to speak on this important issue and how Congress can address the forthcoming challenges we will face. https://t.co/OSQwnpklgn

‘Easy as she goes’ is how we should approach AI in Medicine. We are literally just on the cusp of how this tool can be used. It will never replace human intuition, discernment or compassion. Not quite ready for Prime Time. https://t.co/dzRKeTMmIE
Humans must remain atop the hierarchy. We need to control AI, not the other way around.

Artificial intelligence is at our doorstep and set to explode in just about every industry, including health care. We must protect consumer safety while promoting innovation.

I sent a letter to the FDA Commissioner to ensure we're taking the right steps to prepare: https://t.co/0ooJcbucgV

Artificial intelligence is set to transform health care dramatically, and its emergence in the field of medicine is happening rapidly. As a physician of over 30 years, I am thrilled by the potential of AI to improve the efficiency and quality of patient care in more ways than we could have imagined just ten years ago. We must be judicious in cultivating a regulatory environment that both protects consumers and encourages innovation.

Today, I participated in a roundtable to discuss health AI integration and best practices for implementation.
 
Humans must remain atop the hierarchy and the doctor-patient relationship must be protected.
 
I'm grateful for @WaysandMeansGOP's attention to this exciting technology.

In @WaysandMeansGOP, I questioned IRS Commissioner Werfel on cyber and national security risks surrounding TikTok’s availability on government devices, despite its prohibition. 

I appreciate his commitment to investigate this further and ensure there are no artificial intelligence biases when conducting audits.

I had the pleasure of speaking with Medical Alley, on the transformative potential of AI in American healthcare as well as the obstacles we face ahead.
 
We must erect sensible guardrails that enable innovation and at the same time protect consumers. https://t.co/Z1mAgO42YH

I had a very productive meeting with Siemens Healthineers discussing the explosive growth of artificial intelligence in health care and removing barriers to innovation.   We’ve got a bright future ahead of us with such incredible technology on the horizon. https://t.co/9tZ5vpukuO
This is a pilot, and I'm open to see what's going to happen with this, but I will always, always err on the side that doctors know what's best for their patients.

Team Murphy was proud to attend the unveiling of the Shipcom AI Innovation Lab in Havelock.

The @WaysandMeansGOP Committee held a hearing with IRS CEO Frank Bisignano on the 2026 filing season, agency modernization, and implementation of key tax relief.

I discussed how AI can reduce the 7.1 billion hours Americans spend on tax compliance while ensuring enforcement targets high-dollar tax cheats not working families.

That’s why it was important that the House and Senate unanimously passed my bill, H.R. 1491, the Disaster Related Extension of Deadlines Act, which was signed into law in December, to ensure that taxpayers impacted by natural disasters receive automatic, accurate relief.

It was an honor to speak to the Medical Alley Network about the future of American health care.

As a practicing physician and Co-Chair of the GOP Doctors Caucus, I shared my perspective on how AI is transforming medicine from drug discovery to improving care delivery while emphasizing that humans must always remain in charge.

Innovation must always serve patients, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure it does.
